t: Find the Score Difference in a Game
o: Simulate the rules game by game: before game i, swap the active player if nums[i] is odd, and swap again if i is a multiple-of-6 offset index (5, 11, 17, ...). The active player scores nums[i]. Return player1 total minus player2 total. Example 2 shows both swaps can fire on the same game (index 5 with odd points), swapping twice = net no change before scoring.
k: Both swap rules are checked before the active player scores; they can both trigger on the same game.
A single boolean flag tracks who is active; XOR it for each triggered swap.

a.i: One pass with an active-flag: flip on odd points, flip again on indices i % 6 == 5, then award points. n <= 1000 so nothing fancier is needed.
s: Initialize totals a = b = 0 and active = 0 (first player).
For each i: if nums[i] is odd flip active; if i % 6 == 5 flip active; add nums[i] to the active player's total.

w: Pure simulation; the only traps are applying swaps BEFORE scoring (not after) and remembering both swap rules can co-trigger at index 5, 11, ... Verify against all three examples. Follow-up: what if the every-6th rule fired after scoring, or the odd-swap depended on the running total?
